#1444. RANGERS 3 ABERDEEN 2: Amid all the thrills and spills, McInnes' triple switch sparks second-half revival

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026

When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.

Coming just three days after going out of Europe — for the second time — to an ordinary Jablonec team, the slender win Derek McInnes’ side claimed at Pittodrie that day felt like a can being kicked down the road.

In those early weeks, the players looked lost. The manager admitted that he didn’t know what style of football he was watching. The supporters were preparing for a long, hard winter.

It’s remarkable what can come from one scruffy win on the road. From that point to this, McInnes’ men have now gone 14 games unbeaten in all competitions.

They have the League Cup final to look forward to next month. They are now just one point behind Celtic in the Premiership and look eminently capable of putting in a serious challenge for the title. In keeping with so many performances throughout this run, however, this wasn’t particularly convincing. Flat and rudderless for 45 minutes, Rangers were deservedly a goal behind at the interval.

Credit where it’s due, though. Their response at the outset of the second period was outstanding with three goals coming in 11 minutes courtesy of Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

That ought to have been the platform for many more to follow. But the performance slipped back a level. Aberdeen scored once and could easily have scored again.

Raskin (right) and Gassama celebrate after combining to put Rangers 3-1 up

Naderi capitalises on Muller's mishandling to fire Rangers level at the start of the second half

It was a truly thrilling match, full of slip-ups, incidents and moments of brilliance. The final stages were a tough watch for the home fans who hoped against hope that they’d see their side ease towards a routine victory.

As at Fir Park on Saturday, though, Rangers found a way and added another win to the ledger. And provided that remains the case in the coming weeks and months, none of the light blue legions will be complaining.

Despite ultimately not having quite enough to take something, Aberdeen manager Mario Frick will have been encouraged by much of what he saw here.

Had it not been for that atrocious spell at the outset of the second period, he’d have fancied his men to take something.

They certainly fashioned plenty of opportunities. It was the defensive side of the game which ultimately cost them.

McInnes drafted in Kevin Kelsy, James Penrice and Ben Godfrey with Dujon Sterling, Tuur Rommens and Kim Minsu dropping out. There was a change of shape too, with a switch to a 3-5-2. For the longest time, it did not work.

Lyons gets his head to Marshall's corner to put Aberdeen in front in the first half

While Frick kept faith with the diamond-shaped midfield which served him so well in Ayrshire, he made three changes. In came Ayoub Mouloua, Afeez Aremu and Findlay Marshall at the expense of Hicham Mahou, Ante Palaversa and Stuart Armstrong.

Before the game, there was a minute’s silence in memory of the late, great Ralph Brand. What a pity a couple of clowns in the visiting section were unable to keep their mouths shut for that long.

Rangers started brightly with Penrice’s delivery from the left causing chaos. Dan Neil had a stab at it, then Naderi. Aberdeen survived.

Once Frick’s side settled, Nicky Devlin’s cross was met by Marshall. His header was straight at Ivor Pandur.

Rangers’ general play was broken, their build-up more ponderous than patient. Gassama did manage to drop a shoulder and get a strike away but Aremu’s positioning ensured Marius Muller was untroubled.

Naderi was again Rangers’ most effective player, although the bar was set pretty low initially. The Czech’s lay-off invited Godfrey to let fly. His strike was well off target.

While Gassama got into plenty of promising positions, his crossing continually let him down early on. On the other flank, Badredine Bouanani could not do right for doing wrong.

When the ball broke kindly to Naderi on the edge of the box, Ibrox expected the net to bulge. This time the man of the moment fired over. Rangers’ efforts in the first half were summed up by Naderi being tripped by Gavin Molloy on the edge of the box. Bouanani’s effort from the free-kick was woeful.

Aberdeen were aggressive and organised. And when the moment arose, they went forward in numbers.

McInnes shows his delight after his half-time changes helped turn the game around

They edged in front on the half hour after Marshall won a corner which was a consequence of Frick’s men being prepared to back themselves.

Marshall curled the set-piece deep to the far post. Brad Lyons seemed to be invisible to those in light blue as he made a late run. Olwethu Makhanya belatedly reacted but it was too late.

Lyons got enough on his header to beat Pandur and force Raskin to make the block behind his keeper.

The minute the scoreboard indicated that VAR were checking for a goal, you suspected the Belgian hadn’t done quite enough to keep it out. After a lengthy delay came confirmation of that fact.

How would Rangers respond up until the break? Not terribly well. Lyons’ crude foul on Gassama gave Bouanani a chance to make amends with a set-piece. This one smashed into the wall. Seconds later, the winger fired well over the top when he ought to have done better.

The Dons could easily have doubled their advantage. Jack Milne carried well and rattled the ball into Kevin Nisbet’s feet. The forward played a smart pass around the corner. Mouloua was only denied by a terrific save from Pandur.

There was still time for Mouloua to be thwarted by the outstretched leg of Makhanya as he moved to turn home a cut back.

Bluntly, it was no surprise that McInnes made three changes at the break. Off came Godfrey, Kelsy and Bouanani. On went Minsu, Rommens and Findlay Curtis. The impact was extraordinary.

Re-energised, within 45 seconds Rangers were level. Minsu’s speculative shot did come through heavy traffic. Still, Muller had to hold it. Credit to Naderi for anticipating the fumble. The instant it bounced towards him, he instinctively lashed it home for his 10th of the season. Subdued to that point, the home fans roared their approval. And they’d quickly be off their seats again.

As Aberdeen’s attack broke down, Naderi played a simple pass into space. Gassama had too much pace for the chasing pack. Did he have the finishing? Absolutely. What a turnaround.

Gassama squeezes his shot under Muller to put the home side ahead just after the restart

Two goals in 90 seconds then became three in 11 second-half minutes. Gassama did superbly to motor down the left, look up and play in Raskin. The Belgian smashed the ball back across goal and in.

That should have been that. Yet three minutes later, the Dons were back within a goal of McInnes’ men. Afforded too much time on the left, Alexander Briedl picked out Marshall with his cross. Marshall swept it home with his left foot via the inside of the post.

Remarkably, the Dons might well have levelled. Pandur made a fine save when Minsu threatened to turn an Aberdeen corner into his own net. The ball bounced off Nisbet and just wide.

Terrific throughout, Marshall saw a good strike whistle just wide. The fact the Dons made Rangers sweat for the win will be some consolation.

#1443. Juventus Next Gen beaten 4-0 at Lecco and left third from bottom

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

The opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

The hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He said his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

The table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s plans.

One player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His new contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

Elimoghale was called up to the first-team squad for the first time on 17 September 2026. That call-up came for the opening Europa League league-phase match against NEC.

The next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

The next test comes quickly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

#1440. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

#1439. Feyenoord vs. Ajax - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 20:14, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 20:18

Ajax travel to Feyenoord's De Kuip on Sunday looking to heap further misery on the out-of-form Rotterdam giants in this season's first De Klassieker.

Having previously led the Eredivisie table, Giovanni van Bronckhorst's men have suffered a dramatic decline in form and face the prospect of falling six points behind second-placed De Joden after this weekend's matchweek 14 encounter.

Van Bronckhorst was not in charge of Feyenoord last season, but the returning title-winning manager may fear a repeat of the Stadium Club's collapse given their recent results.

The Rotterdam giants are winless in seven matches across all competitions, including four in the Eredivisie, following a nine-match unbeaten league start that featured seven victories.

De Stadionclub topped the Eredivisie standings after matchweek nine's thrilling 4-3 victory over Telstar, with AZ Alkmaar three points behind and PSV Eindhoven and Ajax trailing by four and five respectively.

Their decline in performances and results is reflected in a four-match winless league run, including defeats in the last two, that has left them fifth, four points behind PSV and three adrift of this weekend's visitors.

With a defence that has failed to keep a clean sheet in five consecutive matches after conceding just once across their previous four top-flight fixtures, Van Bronckhorst's men risk falling further behind if this weekend's results go against them.

De Stadionclub's predicament bears similarities to last season's collapse, when Robin van Persie's side started impressively before fading ahead of Christmas, ultimately costing the former striker his job despite a second-placed finish.

That Feyenoord team ended the campaign 19 points behind PSV after holding a three-point advantage over Peter Bosz's men following the ninth round.

Whether those parallels are being discussed in Rotterdam is anyone's guess, but Ajax will back themselves to increase the pressure on their hosts when they visit De Kuip on Sunday afternoon.

Michel's men remain unbeaten against every Eredivisie opponent except PSV, with the Amsterdam giants collecting 28 points from an available 36 when their defeat to the four-peat-chasing Eindhoven outfit is excluded.

Since losing to Bosz's side in gameweek four, Ajax have dropped points in only three of their subsequent nine matches, claiming maximum points in the other six.

De Joden have notably been almost flawless away from home, remaining unbeaten in six matches and winning five, in contrast to their record at the Johan Cruyff Arena, where they have won only three of seven.

That stark disparity between home and away results may be far from ideal for sustaining a title challenge, but it should give the travelling supporters considerable encouragement ahead of Sunday's trip to Rotterdam.

With Ajax able to finish the weekend top of the standings, trailing PSV by just one point after 13 rounds, the league's strongest away side could be forgiven for targeting a sixth victory on their travels in this season's first De Klassieker.

Feyenoord will assess Jakub Moder (knee) before Sunday's showdown, but Bart Nieuwkoop (knee), Jeremiah St. Juste (leg), Thomas Beelen (broken leg), Tijme Wessels (knee) and Jordan Bos (knee) are sidelined.

After missing last weekend's 3-2 Rotterdam derby defeat to SBV Excelsior through injury, Anis Hadj Moussa returned to the starting XI for the Stadium Club's midweek Champions League loss to Porto and should retain his place.

The Algerian remains a joint-leading scorer for the hosts, who can also call upon summer signing Nacho Ferri (seven goals, three assists), Gjivai Zechiel (five goals, four assists) and Luciano Valente (five goals, two assists).

Tolu Arokodare and Julian Brandt lead Ajax's scoring charts with a combined 13 goals, while Davy Klaassen has contributed a respectable five Eredivisie strikes.

Oscar Gloukh has been a creative force, registering a league-high seven assists in 13 appearances and creating more clear-cut chances (12) than any other player in the division.

Four-goal midfielder Jorthy Mokio suffered a broken leg during the 3-0 victory over ADO Den Haag, ruling him out for around four months.

Kasper Dolberg (ACL) is also a long-term absentee and is expected to miss the remainder of the season, while Viktor Tsygankov, Caio Henrique and Simon Adingra remain sidelined.

Ernst; Read, Kraaijeveld, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Baas, Wijndal; Bissouma, Amrabat, Brandt; Bounida, Arokodare, Gloukh

Feyenoord's failure to keep a clean sheet in five consecutive matches is particularly concerning before facing an Ajax attack boasting Arokodare, Brandt and the division's leading assist provider.

The hosts should create opportunities through their own productive forwards, but the visitors' five wins from six away league games suggest that Michel's men can prevail in an open De Klassieker.

#1438. HIBERNIAN 2 DUNDEE 1: Hibs enjoy some long lost home comfort as Leith men win the battle of the wounded

Published: 18:46 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:51 EST, 24 November 2026

Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.

Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee, still licking their wounds after an 8-0 savaging at the hands of Hearts on Saturday, showed plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Manager Marink Reedijk was thrilled to have bounced back from their 4-0 weekend home defeat at the hands of Dundee United, saying: ‘I think it’s a good reaction to what we have done against Dundee United.

‘It’s important that you get the three points at home. Again, that’s a big win. I saw a front foot team again, I saw togetherness again, I saw a team who fought for every ball.

Martin Boyle takes the acclaim after scoring the all-important second goal for Hibernian

‘That’s not easy, they have to be patient, you have to be secure, you have to wait for your moment and we took these moments and that was really good to see.

‘The goal of Nicky [Cadden] is one to, we say, put in a frame and put on your wall as a painting. The one of Martin [Boyle] is why Martin is so important for us. He can disrupt an opponent if they are so organised and so close to each other and so deep.

‘As long as we keep ourselves, I think these are good signs.’

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend. On a rare start, Togo international Thibault Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan’s lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

Dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them with two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Nicky Cadden unleashes an absolute pearler into the top corner to put Hibs in front

Cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Steven Pressley’s side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones’ free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

For Pressley, who changed half of his outfield XI following his side’s weekend humiliation, there were also positives to take.

The Dark Blues boss said: ‘We’re disappointed to not come away with anything and to obviously lose the game. But I also thought we restored some degree of pride tonight.

‘Going into half-time 2-0 down, losing two late goals in the half, can be a little bit demoralising, especially for a team that has a bit of fragility on the back of the weekend’s result.

‘I thought we responded brilliantly. We showed a lot of courage, a lot of determination, a lot of spirit and, as I’ve said, I think we certainly restored some level of pride that allows us a foundation to move into the weekend.’

#1436. Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews said. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”

Brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa said: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”

9 - Florian Wirtz's nine chances created from open play against Brentford is the most by a player in a Premier League game since Sadio Mané v Burnley in January 2021 (9) and the most by a player in an away game since Samir Nasri v Spurs in August 2011 (10). Progress. https://t.co/xyMIQP9y5p

The red card was the turning point in this game but the £400m frontline have delivered what was expected of them since the break.

Brentford 1 Liverpool 2 (Isak) The Swede is only just back from injury, and in all fairness has not looked great for much of this afternoon, but he’s put Liverpool infront here. Mac Allister plays a one-two with Wirtz down the right and the ball is worked to Barcola at the far post. The France winger nods it into the path of Isak who composes himself before spearing the ball beyond Kelleher.

Hull haven’t given up the ghost at Craven Cottage, knowing how easily Fulham crumbled last time out. Belloumi tries his luck from distance but cannot find the target.

Superb finish by Victor Munoz to level the scores here. Brentford were caught upfield and they were in trouble from the moment Florian Wirtz was able to slide the ball in behind for the Spanish winger. It comes as Liverpool were just starting to make their numerical advantage count.

Manchester City 3 Ipswich Town 1 (Haaland) Ndiaye does well to play in Haaland who breezes past Outtara before lacing the ball into the bottom corner.

Brentford 1 Liverpool 1 (Munoz) Ngumoha plays the ball infield to Wirtz on the half-way line, and the German threads a ball in behind for the rapid Munoz to gallop on to, he cuts inside Lewis-Potter and fires the ball beyond Kelleher with his left foot.

Iwobi goes close. His curled effort has Tzolakis scrambling but zips just wide of the mark.

Fernandez, on as a second-half substitute, tries his luck with a free-kick from 25 yards out, but he cannot get the requisite dip on the ball to bring it down and it flies over.

Fulham are still dominating the ball and have been by far the better side. Their possession share remains in the high seventies. They’ve completed 476 passes to Hull’s 94.

A second goal would surely put this one to bed.

Liverpool brought on Jeremie Frimpong as a half-time substitute but he’s already limped off. That’s the second injury they have picked up today, after Dominik Szoboszlai.

This is a proper test of Liverpool’s creative ability now. Ten-man Brentford are going to sit deep for most of this second half, I am sure. Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola... time to deliver some game-changing quality.

Jacquet goes into the book. A loose pass out from the back is picked off my Brentford substitute Schade and Jacquet snaps in too enthusiastically and receives a yellow.

Chance! Will Fulham rue all these missed chances? King is involved once more, standing up a cross to the back post where Garcia nods down for Iwobi to stroke goalwards near the penalty spot, but Tzolakis does well to get down low to his left and keep Fulham’s advantage to just one goal.

Mateo Kovacic comes off injured for City. It is probably just a knock as he’s sat on the bench rather than heading down the tunnel. Was a standout player in the first half.

Close! Ajayi’s clearance comes straight back and Charles works the ball to King on the right, but with just the keeper to beat, the midfielder’s effort is saved by Tzolakis with his feet. King really should be scoring there.

Still some time before the Liverpool game resumes given the time added on at the end of the first half.

Following his clash of heads with Jarrad Branthwaite in the lunchtime kick-off at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, the Chelsea goalkeeper has now been taken to hospital to undergo precautionary tests.

Brentford lead Liverpool thanks to Keane Lewis-Potter's header, but the second half could be tricky for the Bees after Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off just before half-time. Liverpool are yet to have a shot on target despite having seven shots in the first half. #BRELIV https://t.co/o9HE2Fh8qb

Andrews will be furious with how that first half ended. His side had done brilliantly to establish a lead, but will have their work cut out keeping Liverpool out after the break with the visitors a man to the good.

With half-time fast approaching and Brentford in front, this is absolute madness. Yarmoliuk looks to have butted Jacquet in an incident that reminds of Bentacur’s red card at Old Trafford last weekend.

The referee is sent to the pitchside monitor after a lengthy delay and Yarmoliuk is off!

We’ve had the second VAR review in just a few minutes here, and this one has resulted in a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk for a “headbutting action”. I have to say, this feels harsh. It’s pretty tame. There is a tiny movement towards Jacquet, who collapsed to the turf in dramatic fashion, but he’s hardly caused the Liverpool defender any damage. That will change the dynamic of this game.

Haaland restores City’s lead after Maeda had cancelled out Foden’s opener.

Arbeloa’s side are in front and could have been ahead by a wider margin, but we’ve been here before...

Gary Neville is a w-----, is a w-----.....is quite a loud chant here at City. Fans in a good mood here after Erling Haaland scored in his eighth game in a row.

Brentford 1 Liverpool 0 (Lewis-Potter) Outtara curls in a wonderful cross and Lewis-Potter steals in to head the ball beyond Alisson from 10 yards out.

Brentford take the lead, and it’s a lead they probably just about deserve on the run of play. It’s an absolutely superb header by Keane Lewis-Potter, up from left-back, as he thumps Igor Thiago’s cross into the top corner of Liverpool’s net. Textbook technique.

Just after Wirtz was denied a penalty of his own, Mac Allister looks to have won a spot-kick for real off a challenge from Outtara. The referee gives it, but is then sent to the monitor and the decision is reversed. Correct decision. Outtara clearly got a piece of the ball first.

Liverpool have been awarded a penalty but I don’t think this will stand. It shouldn’t stand. Dango Ouattara got a touch on the ball when he lunged in on Alexis Mac Allister.

Yep, the penalty has been overturned. Referee John Brooks missed Outtara’s touch on first viewing but the replays were pretty conclusive.

Manchester City 2 Ipswich Town 1 (Haaland) Kovacic wriggles free of his markers and darts to the by-line. He’s able to stand up a cross and Haaland heads the ball forcefully downwards - just as your grassroots football coach always told you to - and Walton is unable to keep it out. Probably should have done better.

Fulham 1 Hull City 0 (Iwobi) A big, big goal for Fulham and Arbeloa. They are finally able to convert their overwhelming dominance with the ball into something material. This goal comes at the end of a sweeping move, with Iwobi stroking the ball beyond Tzolakis, who probably should have done better.

Bradley Barcola may not be justifying his fee at Liverpool yet but another Frenchman, Jeremy Jacquet, certainly is. The centre-back has been excellent all season and he has just produced a goal-saving challenge on Brentford’s Igor Thiago. A sliding tackle, perfectly timed, just as Thiago was about to score.

Brentford are getting the ball forward quickly, and Kelleher is the one to initiate the latest move. He finds Thiago on the halfway line, who gets the ball back off Outtara, but the Brazilian’s effort is well blocked by Van Dijk.

Some bad news for Liverpool, though, as Szoboszlai sits on the turf. It looks like his afternoon might already be over.

Daizen Maeda showed good strength to hold off Marc Guehi’s challenge before scoring his first goal for Ipswich since signing from Celtic. City will be disappointed with the defending there - it was a straightforward ball down the channel from Abdoul Ouattara.

Before that Phil Foden sent a message to Thomas Tuchel with the opening goal. Foden, playing in central midfield, was left out of the last England squad and has seen Alex Scott climb above him in the pecking order. But Scott is injured for next month’s international which may give Foden a chance.

Was Bradley Barcola’s midweek hat-trick the start of a great run of form for the £123m forward? Not on this evidence. A defensive mix-up allowed the Frenchman a clear run at goal, one-on-one with Brentford’s Caoimhin Kelleher, but his finish was woeful. An attempted dink that bobbled harmlessly wide. “What a waste of money,” comes the cry from the Brentford fans.

Manchester City 1 Ipswich Town 1 (Maeda) Woah, barely a minute between these two goals at the Etihad. Guehi relinquishes possession to Maeda and, left alone in the box, he stears the ball into the far bottom corner.

Manchester City 1 Ipswich Town 0 (Foden) While Foden has scored, huge credit must go to Doku, who did brilliantly down the left, working the ball on to his right foot before squaring to Foden who gets a shot away - Walton does well to get a hand on the ball, but he cannot keep it out.

Liverpool are looking bright, with Barcola and Wirtz combining well - just as they did in midweek - to force a corner. The ball is worked to Mac Allister on the edge of the box but his effort sails well over.

“You’re going down with the City,” sing the home fans at the Ipswich travelling support.

Arbeloa’s side have dominated the ball thus far, claiming an 87 per cent share of the ball. Hull have completed a grand total of 14 passes. But this has been the story of their season so far, lots of the ball but very little incision. Let’s see if they can be more productive this afternoon.

Bright start by Brentford here, although Liverpool have just created their first chance of the game as Szoboszlai shoots over from the edge of the box.

Thiago is putting himself about in Liverpool’s box, winning a corner which is headed behind for another by Van Dijk, but it comes to nothing.

Liverpool break and their sweeping move up the field comes to Wirtz whose cut-back picks out Szoboszlai perfectly but the midfielder miscues and his effort does not trouble Kelleher.

Ipswich centre-back Issa Diop did not take the knee like the other players on the pitch just before kick-off here at the Etihad Stadium. The Premier League’s ‘No Room For Racism’ initiative is this weekend and players have been invited to kneel on the pitch. Some players believe taking the knee has lost its meaning and impact.

As expected, Ipswich have dropped into a deep five-man block with very little space between their lines. It will be up to City’s creative players to fashion chances this afternoon.

Fulham simply need to win today and they get off to a good start. Iwobi goes close with an early effort which is turned behind by Tzolakis.

Huge boos and whistles for the Premier League anthem at the Etihad Stadium, with the final part of it drowned out by chants of “City, City, City.” Fans have made their feelings clear after the guilty verdict from the competition’s independent commission, with the club appealing the decision.

The anthem never gets a warm reception here - but that is the loudest I’ve heard the dissent.

It’s back-to-back wins for Chelsea and a rare clean sheet, their first since January. But all thoughts will be with Emi Martinez after his clash of heads with Branthwaite. Hopefully we get some good news on that front soon. Follow the latest updates here.

There is also a place for Phil Foden after serving his three-match ban for getting dismissed in the Manchester derby.

Keith Andrews has established a clearly defined, direct style of play which speaks to Brentford’s strengths. His side are third in the Premier League for percentage of passes forward (39.2 per cent) and, coupled with the second-most high turnovers which end in a goal, Brentford have thrived off passages of organised chaos.

To play this way requires quality when you do have the ball, and full-backs Keane Lewis-Potter and Michael Kayode deserve particular praise. They have contributed materially to Brentford’s attacks, helping their side to league-high successful crosses (26) and expected goals from set-pieces (4.03).

A re-examination of Abu Dhabi government documents, receipts and testimony from 24 witnesses – all of which the club believe were wrongly dismissed at the original hearing – will be central in attempts to force a full or partial acquittal or retrial, according to people familiar with the case.

City’s legal team will attempt to demonstrate “fundamental errors” in tests applied by an independent commission to the Premier League’s case that commercial revenue was artificially inflated by £920m. Shahid Khan, Fulham’s owner, insists that his team are on a “positive path” despite remaining winless in the Premier League after six matches.

In his programme notes, he wrote: “I want to reflect on our recent form. Prior to the international break, we were trending upward… That momentum carried us through most of Saturday’s match at Ipswich Town, but we all know how that ended. The result was devastating for all of us, and I won’t pretend otherwise.

“And yet, I am reminded of the positive path we have been on and the genuine potential of this team. Our squad is strong, while still coming together. We have been in every match, missing only the opportunities we’ve had to complete the task. I believe those opportunities will soon be seized.”

The good news for Liverpool is that Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai are fit enough to start the game, and that Brentford top scorer Kevin Schade is not. Schade is on the bench after picking up a shoulder injury against Aston Villa last weekend.

“It’s remarkable because to score three goals in a Champions League game is … not a lot of players can say they have done it.

“It’s something nice for him but I think the best thing is we can feel him, he seems with confidence on the ball [away] from the goals, straight away you could feel he was confident going in one-to-one situations, attacking the spaces and [those] are his strengths.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca said in his pre-match press conference.”

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”

Ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

Elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be said for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

Pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

#1434. Lazio lose Tavares and Sutalo for at least three weeks as Juventus chase 11-point gap

Defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence. The setback hits Gattuso's back line just as Juventus return from the break chasing the leaders.

Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow. Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo were both injured in the 1-1 draw at Napoli. The timing is awkward for the leaders, who resume their league campaign against Lecce on 21 November.

Exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete. The early estimate is about 20 days for each player, Sky Sport Italia reported. On that timeline, both miss the home game against Lecce and could return for the trip to Torino on 28 November.

Not every report is that hopeful. Football Italia reported that the pair should miss both the Lecce and Torino games. Under that scenario, they hope to be available again in the first week of December. The match against Atalanta on 6 December is also in doubt.

Tavares has been a real attacking outlet this season. He has one goal and four assists in 11 Serie A games. He also has a long record of muscle injuries. Sutalo has made eight league appearances since joining on loan from Ajax on 22 August.

Lazio must now turn to their alternatives. Alfonso Pedraza, who joined from Villarreal in the summer, is the leading option at left-back. He has played 322 minutes across the league and Coppa Italia. Diogo Leite and Doekhi are competing to replace Sutalo in the middle.

The stand-ins inherit a strong record. Lazio have scored 25 goals and conceded 9 so far. Keeping that defensive record with a reshuffled back line is now Gattuso’s task.

Juventus know Lazio’s quality first-hand. Gattuso’s side won 3-0 in Turin earlier this season. That result still weighs on the table. Five wins, three draws and three defeats make up the Juventus record from their opening games.

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 8, 2026

Two missing defenders will not close the gap on their own. They do, however, give Juventus a window in which the leaders are weaker than usual. Any dropped points by Lazio over the coming rounds would only count if Juventus take care of their own fixtures.

Those fixtures follow Lazio’s closely. Como v Juventus is scheduled for Sunday 29 November at 20:45, the day after Lazio’s game against Torino. Further ahead, Lazio’s aim is to have both defenders fit for the Rome derby on 13 December.

#1433. Brighton & Hove Albion vs Newcastle United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 27 Nov 2026 22:17

Brighton & Hove Albion will be looking to maintain the pressure at the top of the Premier League table when they host Newcastle United at the American Express Stadium on Sunday.

The Seagulls have surprised many with their rise to second place, sitting six points behind leaders Arsenal, while the Magpies are down in 13th, just four points clear of the relegation zone.

Brighton have made tremendous progress under Fabian Hurzeler and have emerged as surprise contenders in the Premier League title race, at least during the early stages of the season.

They suffered just their third defeat of the season in a 2-0 loss to Hull City in their previous match, missing the opportunity to close the gap on the Gunners to three points.

What has been particularly impressive is their scintillating attacking style, with Hurzeler's side having scored 26 goals already, more than any other team in the division.

The Seagulls have also been formidable on home soil, collecting four wins and a draw from their five matches at the American Express Stadium, scoring 15 goals and conceding just once.

They head into this game on the back of a thumping 4-0 victory over Universitatea Craiova in the Europa Conference League on Thursday, with confidence clearly flowing through the squad.

Newcastle, in contrast, have endured a difficult season and find themselves closer to the relegation zone than the European places.

Matthias Jaissle's side have managed just three league victories so far, while suffering four defeats.

The Magpies are winless in their last three Premier League matches and have gone four games without a victory across all competitions, including a 3-1 defeat to Everton in the EFL Cup.

The Tyneside club, however, have picked up two wins on the road this season, although they have managed just one victory in their last six league outings.

Newcastle will nevertheless be buoyed by their impressive second-half performance against Arsenal last time out, when they held the champions to a 2-2 draw.

Costinha is suspended for this game following his late red card last weekend and could be replaced at right-back by Mats Wieffer, while Olivier Boscagli could also return at left-back after recovering from illness.

Hurzeler could drop Georginio Rutter, with Charalampos Kostoulas potentially returning to the starting XI after being relegated to the bench against Hull.

Brighton are missing a host of players, with Jaouen Hadjam, Stefanos Tzimas, Evan Ferguson, Kaoru Mitoma, Malick Yalcouye and Zadok Yohanna all sidelined through injury, while Femi Azeez is doubtful for the game.

The Magpies remain without goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, who is currently nursing a hamstring injury and is not expected to return before mid-December.

Joelinton is also struggling with a thigh injury, and although no definitive timeline has been set for his return, the Brazilian is likely to be back at the start of next month.

Brighton & Hove Albion possible starting lineup:

Newcastle United possible starting lineup:

Brighton remain unbeaten at home this season and will be eager to get back to winning ways, particularly after their shock defeat to Hull City.

The Magpies have not won away at Brighton since claiming a 2-1 victory in the Championship in February 2017, and we back the Seagulls to extend that run and secure all three points.

#1432. Thuram and Locatelli absences leave Juventus midfield thin for four games in 12 days

Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

The table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

#1429. Crystal Palace vs. Hull City: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 23:08

Crystal Palace host Hull City at Selhurst Park on Sunday looking to build on their midweek European victory and claim a first Premier League win since early October.

Bottom-placed Palace have kept just one clean sheet in 11 matches and Thomas Frank will be keen to shore up the division's leakiest defence as the Eagles bid to climb out of the relegation zone.

Visitors Hull City arrive in buoyant mood after ending a three-month wait for a top-flight victory against Brighton & Hove Albion, with Sergej Jakirovic's 11th-placed Tigers eyeing consecutive wins to push into the top half.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Crystal Palace and Hull.

Across 54 previous meetings between Crystal Palace and Hull City in all competitions, it is actually the Tigers who boast the superior historical record, having claimed 20 victories compared to the Eagles' 16.

Another 18 contests have finished all square, including an absorbing 3-3 draw in East Yorkshire during the 2016-17 Premier League season, when Fraizer Campbell struck an 89th-minute equaliser to rescue a point for the visitors.

When the pair last crossed paths five months later in May 2017, however, it was one-way traffic at Selhurst Park, as goals from Wilfried Zaha, Christian Benteke, Luka Milivojevic and Patrick van Aanholt sealed a 4-0 rout that secured Palace's top-flight survival and consigned Hull to relegation.

That emphatic victory gave the capital club a narrow 3-2 edge across their six Premier League showdowns to date, with both sides having previously traded league doubles — Palace edging to back-to-back 1-0 wins in 2013-14 courtesy of Barry Bannan and Jason Puncheon before Hull replied with twin 2-0 triumphs in 2014-15.

Indeed, the modern era has heavily favoured the South Londoners, who have lost just four of their last 22 meetings with Hull in all competitions since October 1988, winning 10 and drawing eight in that spell.

Prior to their top-flight clashes, the duo were regular Championship foes between 2005 and 2013, yet the Tigers managed only a single victory across 12 second-tier encounters — a 2-1 home win in April 2008 — while seven ended in a share of the spoils and Palace registered four successes, highlighted by a 4-2 triumph in March 2013 featuring a Kevin Phillips hat-trick.

Furthermore, Selhurst Park has long proved an unforgiving venue for Hull, whose 2-0 win in April 2015 via a Dame N'Doye double represents their only triumph in 13 visits to South London since October 1985.

Hull's overall advantage was therefore largely forged during the fixture's earlier decades, having won 16 of the first 32 meetings between 1921 and 1987 — including 5-0 and 6-1 thrashings in the old Division Two — while the Tigers also boast the upper hand in cup ties, overcoming Palace in the FA Cup in 1921 and 1925 before progressing on away goals after a 2-2 aggregate draw in the 1997-98 League Cup despite losing the second leg 2-1.

#1428. Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

#1427. Hoffenheim vs Augsburg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 27 Nov 2026 23:14, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 23:22

Hoffenheim will be looking to build on their impressive comeback win over Sturm Graz in the Europa League when they welcome Augsburg to the SNP Arena this Sunday evening.

Consistency has been a big issue for Die Kraichgauer in recent weeks, while the visitors recently snapped a seven-match winless run in the Bundesliga.

Balancing domestic and European duties has proved difficult for Hoffenheim, who have endured a mixed start to the season.

Christian Ilzer’s men enter the weekend 11th in the standings after losing six of their 10 Bundesliga games, equalling their club record for defeats at this stage of a campaign.

November has been more encouraging, however, with Hoffenheim drawing away at Crystal Palace, losing at Eintracht Frankfurt and winning their last two home games against Schalke and Sturm Graz.

Thursday’s victory over the Austrian side was particularly impressive, as Hoffenheim came from behind to win 3-1 and move within three points of the Europa League’s top eight.

That was also their fourth consecutive home victory, with three of those wins seeing them score exactly three goals.

While the hosts are beginning to build momentum, Ilzer faces some difficult selection decisions after injuries and suspensions decimated his defence, leaving him with just one natural centre-back.

Augsburg may not be flying high in the Bundesliga table, but they have at least found themselves among the league’s elite in one rather unexpected ranking.

Manuel Baum’s side sit second according to online portal Bild Dating’s AI-generated beauty leaderboard, which rates the attractiveness of every squad in the German top flight.

Their on-field fortunes have been a lot less glamorous, though a 3-1 victory over Mainz 05 last time out lifted Augsburg to 10th in the actual standings and brought an end to their seven-game winless run in the Bundesliga.

The win over Mainz also saw Baum receive a straight red card for delaying play in the second half - a punishment which will see him rooted to the stands on Sunday.

Assistants Alexander Frankenberger, Frank Frohling and Felix Kling will share touchline duties in Hoffenheim as Augsburg look to claim just their second win in 11 meetings with the Kraichgauer.

The trio will take charge of a youthful Augsburg side that made club history against Mainz, fielding their youngest-ever starting XI with an average age of just 23.7 years.

Six players in the team were aged 21 or under - a stat which underlines the extent of the club’s ongoing injury problems and the responsibility placed on their young talents.

Hoffenheim’s main concern is the suspension of Ozan Kabak, who received a four-match ban for grabbing Eintracht Frankfurt’s Oscar Hojlund by the scruff of the neck and pushing him to the ground.

Hoffenheim have lodged an appeal, though Kabak remains suspended from league action until Friday’s hearing, where the punishment may be cut short or potentially extended.

This is a massive blow for Ilzer, who is already missing four other defensive players in Wouter Burger (muscle), Valentin Gendrey (broken leg), Albian Hajdari (foot) and Robin Hranac (knee).

In fact, Japan’s Koki Machida remains the only available natural centre-back in the squad.

Augsburg are also dealing with a lengthy injury list, although Calvin Brackelmann is available again after returning from his absence.

However, Han-Noah Massengo and Jeffrey Gouweleeuw remain out of action with muscular problems, while an infection has disrupted Noakhai Banks’ recovery.

Chrislain Matsima is making progress from a torn muscle but is not yet ready to return, potentially opening the door for 18-year-old Tim Schnitzer to retain his place after impressing against Mainz.

Baumann; Coufal, Machida, Bernardo, Rots; Avdullahu, Lenz; Conte, Asllani, Prass; Lemperle

Dahmen; Keitel, Bah, Schnitzer; Fellhauer, Wolf, Rieder, Behrens; Kade, Claude-Maurice; Gregoritsch

Hoffenheim have defensive concerns, but their formidable home record against Augsburg should give them confidence, having lost just one of their last 15 Bundesliga meetings on their own ground.

Augsburg, meanwhile, have lost their last three away league games and, with several senior players unavailable, could struggle to avoid another defeat against their bogey team.

Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. Çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

#1419. Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 17:22 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 24 November 2026

Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious issue.

It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.

When Kepa Arrizabalaga parried Julian Ryerson's shot into the path of Jobe Bellingham, the Arsenal script had seemingly flipped from first-half domination to second-half capitulation.

Luckily for Mikel Arteta, Bellingham's tap-in was flagged for offside to keep the north London club's unbeaten record in this competition intact, stretching back to 20 matches (excluding penalty shootouts).

Earlier in the second half, Maximilian Beier had equalised, skilfully turning Gabriel before placing a neat strike past Kepa.

But this match should have been sealed well before then for Arsenal - and they had enough chances to win it late on, too. Viktor Gyokeres headed wide when unmarked and Declan Rice struck the woodwork.

Arsenal were made to pay for their complacency again by drawing with Borussia Dortmund

Arsenal were held 1-1 with Dortmund thanks to this Maximilian Beier's strike for the visitors

By full-time, the Gunners had mustered 30 shots, but no winning goal.

Despite his team's wastefulness, Arteta said: 'The domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more. I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.'

But the recurrence of losing concentration later in matches, as the Gunners did against Slavia Prague and Newcastle in recent weeks, is an issue which Arteta must urgently address.

It is not sustainable, and ruined an evening initially lit up by Gyokeres' stunning strike. The Sweden striker's display reflected the fierce competition for places at Arsenal. Perform well and you have a chance of a starting spot. Anything less results in a place on the bench in the winter's cold.

Gyokeres received Noni Madueke's pass outside the area on ten minutes and Dortmund's back line completely backed off, almost pleading for him to shoot.

He obliged, cocking his right boot back to unleash a powerful strike which initially looked to be going over the bar before dipping into goalkeeper Gregor Kobel's net. It was a top-drawer finish from a man who cannot nail down a regular starting spot, despite 21 goals last season and a goal and assist in Arsenal's previous Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

It is the kind of luxury Arteta has worked towards since taking on this job seven years ago.

One back-up player who inspires rather less confidence is goalkeeper Kepa. No1 David Raya injured his shoulder at Newcastle and so in came his fellow Spaniard. Kepa's touches early on were cheered by the Arsenal faithful, massaging the confidence of a man who has endured the kind of calamity which is not easily erased from memory.

The dropping of Rayan Cherki's cross in March's Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City; his lapse to misjudge a corner and gift Real Betis a goal during pre-season - these are the sorts of errors which have Arsenal fans feeling uncomfortable whenever Raya is unavailable.

Viktor Gyokeres (left) opened the scoring with this stunning long-range strike for the Gunners

Kepa Arrizabalaga (right) started in goal for Arsenal with first-choice David Raya out injured

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Arrizabalaga 6; White 6 (Timber 65, 6), Konsa 6, Gabriel 5, Hincapie 6; Lewis-Skelly 5 (Guimaraes 66, 6), Rice 7; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 66, 6); Gyokeres 7.

Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel 6; Gadou 7, Anton 6, Schlotterbeck 6; Ryerson 6, Nmecha 6, Veerman 6, Svensson 6; Bellingham 6, Beier 7 (Guirassy 65, 6); Fabio Silva 6 (Karetsas 65, 6).

Raya is battling to return for Arsenal's huge Premier League clash against Manchester City on Sunday and the sense of panic in the days after his injury has been understandable.

Raya is so much more than just an excellent shot-stopper. His distribution is second to none: pinpoint long throws to set wingers away on counter-attacks and a highly impressive passing range, both aerially and across the floor.

Still, Kepa just about survived. There were jitters, like passing the ball straight to a yellow shirt on 52 minutes, which the opposition failed to punish. But he hung in there and that will have given his confidence a boost.

Arsenal started well, Madueke continuing his excellent form of late in place of the injured Bukayo Saka. Madueke crossed for Christos Tzolis, who drove his shot into the turf, before setting up Martin Odegaard to shoot wide.

It didn't take long for the winger's passing to produce results, as he fed Gyokeres for that venomous strike from distance.

Rice lashed a strike from range which dipped just over the bar as Dortmund showed a tendency to gift too much time on the ball.

After the break Dortmund changed tack. Sitting back and soaking up the pressure was not working, so they got the ball forward more quickly and more often, forcing Arsenal on to the back foot.

The Gunners held on for a point - and endured another lesson in switching off.

#1417. Juventus sell out Venezia game as Omonia sales pass 35,000

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

General sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

This season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

The Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

By Nsidibe Akpan | 27 Nov 2026 23:58

Fortuna Sittard play host to SC Heerenveen in the 2026-27 Eredivisie at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion in Sittard on Sunday.

Heerenveen are sixth on the Eredivisie table on 24 points and Fortuna seventh on 23, with leaders PSV Eindhoven on 29, so Sunday's winner will leave a direct rival for one of the European play-off places trailing in December.

Danny Buijs's side have lost only twice in 13 league games and are unbeaten in seven since a 5-1 home defeat by Ajax on September 12, leaving the Fortunezen seventh on 23 points from six wins, five draws and two defeats.

Both of those defeats, the other being 2-0 against AZ on August 22 with Ole Romeny sent off early, came at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion, whereas Fortuna are unbeaten away from home, with a 1-1 draw at Feyenoord on October 31 featuring an equaliser from Feyenoord loanee Shiloh 't Zand.

Home draws have been the problem, as Fortuna led Twente 1-0 on October 10 through an Anthony Descotte header from a Mohamed Ihattaren cross before drawing 1-1, and led Telstar 2-0 on November 7 through an Ihattaren penalty and a Sem Valk own goal before conceding twice before half time in a 2-2 draw.

Their latest home win was a 1-0 victory over Excelsior on October 25, decided by a Rodrigo Guth header from an Ihattaren corner in stoppage time, when Descotte and Lequincio Zeefuik were unavailable and Ihattaren started on the bench.

The most recent result was a 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles on November 22, when Descotte scored his sixth goal of the season in the 50th minute after Ihattaren sent substitute Kristoffer Peterson clear, ending the hosts' unbeaten home record.

Off the pitch, Buijs announced on Wednesday, November 18 that he will not extend a contract expiring in 2027 and will leave after four seasons, which leaves Fortuna a little over six months to appoint a successor.

Robin Veldman's De Superfriezen have won their last six matches in all competitions, including five straight in the league against Excelsior (4-0), ADO Den Haag (3-2), NEC Nijmegen (1-0), Feyenoord (5-3) and Groningen (3-1), scoring 16 goals and conceding six.

The 5-3 win over Feyenoord on November 8 ended the leaders' unbeaten league record, with Heerenveen recovering from 2-0 down after 31 minutes through Maas Willemsen, Levi Smans and a hat-trick from half-time substitute Ringo Meerveld in the 61st, 84th and 93rd minutes.

At Groningen on November 21, Dylan Vente scored in the 41st minute after a blunder by goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar and again in the 73rd, with substitute Dirk Proper adding a third in the 80th to secure a first win at the Euroborg since March 19, 2023.

Heerenveen's 27 goals scored and 17 conceded give them a goal difference of +10, nine better than Fortuna's +1 from 21 scored and 20 conceded.

The run followed a September wobble that ended with a 4-0 win at Sparta Rotterdam on September 19 after a five-game winless spell, and the only league defeat since was 2-0 at PSV Eindhoven on October 9.

Heerenveen have also won their last two league games on the road, 3-2 at ADO Den Haag on October 24, when Jacob Trenskow scored twice, and 3-1 at Groningen.

Fortuna have a goalkeeping problem, as first-choice Mattijs Branderhorst sprained an ankle in training before the Go Ahead game and Luuk Koopmans, who made several saves in that 1-0 win, is expected to deputise again.

Buijs is also without attackers Zeefuik and Romeny, who are both expected back around January 8, plus midfielder Edouard Michut, who is due back around December 5, and defender Daley Sinkgraven.

The losses matter because Descotte, Zeefuik and Ihattaren had scored 11 of Fortuna's first 16 league goals before the Excelsior game, which leaves Descotte, Sven Simons and Peterson to carry the attack.

Yassin Oukili is a doubt after a spell out, and Buijs is expected to keep the back-five shape used at Deventer.

Heerenveen have one doubt in defender Hristiyan Petrov, who returned from Bulgaria duty injured, missed the Groningen derby and was still not fully fit on Friday, when Veldman said the club would decide whether he travels.

The rest of the squad trained on Friday morning without problems, no suspensions have been reported, and Veldman is likely to keep the side that won at Groningen, with Mees Hilgers covering at centre-back if Petrov is not risked.

Koopmans; Van Ottele, Guth, Hubner, Pinto, Dahlhaus; Ihattaren, Brittijn, 't Zand; Simons, Descotte

Klaverboer; Braude, Kersten, Willemsen, Zagaritis; Linday, Courtens; Trenskow, Smans, Meerveld; Vente

Heerenveen have scored three or more goals in four of their last five league games and field five forwards of their own in Vente, Meerveld, Trenskow, Smans and Rivera, whereas Fortuna have lost Zeefuik and Romeny and lean heavily on Descotte and Ihattaren for goals.

Fortuna's unbeaten run and their record of two or more goals in four of the last five meetings cannot be ignored, but they have won only two of six home league games, twice surrendered a lead against Twente and Telstar, and will start a stand-in goalkeeper against a side that has scored 16 goals in its last five league games.

Five of the last six meetings have produced at least three goals, including Heerenveen's 2-1 win on April 25, 2026 and Fortuna's 2-0 win on November 8, 2025, so Descotte should score again, but Heerenveen's depth and momentum make them the likelier side to land the decisive second.

#1413. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.
