Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and said he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

With all eyes on the visitors, Leeds will be licking their lips at the prospect of piling further misery on their beleaguered opponents. Daniel Farke’s side suffered their first Premier League loss last weekend, falling 2-1 to Arsenal at the Emirates after going a goal up, but the mood remains positive after a solid start to the campaign.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

This has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1383. FIFA: UEFA unanimously supports Philippe Diallo against Infantino

UEFA has officially given its support to Philippe Diallo. In a press release published this Monday, the European body confirms that the national associations represented within its executive committee and the FIFA Council have unanimously invited the president of the French Football Federation to run in the next FIFA presidential election, scheduled for March 2027. The meeting, chaired by Aleksander Ceferin, thus made it possible to validate the choice of the French leader to run the European candidacy against Gianni Infantino. The European body clearly displayed its position in its press release. “The European national associations represented on the UEFA Executive Committee and the FIFA Council unanimously support Philippe Diallo for the presidency of FIFA. At a meeting held today and chaired by UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the UEFA Executive Committee and the FIFA Council invited Philippe Diallo, President of the French Football Federation (FFF), to put himself forward as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously expressed their full support.specifies the press release.

“Philippe Diallo has extensive experience at all levels of football, having led the organization representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of directors of the French Professional Football League and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023. Philippe Diallo accepted the invitation to stand. His candidacy should be formally ratified by the FFF Executive Committee at its meeting tomorrow», It is written in the rest of the missive. The president of the FFF must now have his candidacy validated by the executive committee of his federation.

#1382. Alguacil reveals conviction regarding how Olympiacos could have beaten Milan

Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil believes that his side would have beaten AC Milan had they hung on a bit longer before conceding.

Everything was going according to plan for the Greek side when Lorenzo Pirola’s header hit the bar then Mike Maignan and nestled in to put them a goal up, before Jota Silva fired in a second following Koni De Winter’s stray pass out from the back.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With Milan’s Europa League hopes in need of revival, Omari Hutchinson stepped up with a masterclass. He gave Ruben Amorim’s side hope with a fine individual effort, then he set up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser and Christian Pulisic for the go-ahead goal, before Diego Moreira sealed it.

It was therefore a bittersweet night for Alguacil, one in which his side showed they can dominate one of the big names in the competition, but ultimately emerging empty-handed. He analysed the game in a post-match press conference which MilanNews attended.

The team showed what they could do for 60 minutes. How can you explain what happened?

“At a key moment in the match, we went from a possible 3-0 lead to 2-1, and our confidence crumbled. Milan reacted well: they’re stronger, they have experience, they’re a historic team, and if you’re not focused, you risk losing, as happened.

“Milan gave it their all, but until the 60th minute, we played a great match, like a Champions League team.”

Are you satisfied with the defence’s performance? Is this formation likely to continue going forward?

“I don’t know. A coach has to find solutions, especially because it depends on how we recover our players. We have some out, others played today, and we’ll see the consequences.

“We’ll see who I have available, also thinking about the next match, but Olympiacos, despite the change in formation, played very well.

“We played well, took the lead, deserved the 3-0, and I’m convinced that if we had held on to a 2-0 lead for a few more minutes, we would have won. The 2-4 scoreline seems unfair to me.”

Five players out, but the team still proved to be strong. Is there a chance you can directly advance to the last 16 and go deeper?

“I don’t know where the limit is, I don’t have a definitive answer. I’ll try to get the most out of the team. The lads are training hard, and it’s unfair to have conceded these four goals. In the end, we lacked energy. Milan are a Champions League team, very technical, but I’ll hold on to these 65 minutes.

“We played better than Milan, and I’ll try to make it impossible to play this hour of play again in the next games. By doing so, it will be easier for us to win.”

#1381. Neto set for first Juventus game since 2017 and says his Turin chapter was still open

Norberto Neto is set for his first competitive game in almost six months when Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday night. Speaking on the eve of the match, the 37 year old goalkeeper said he still felt he had unfinished business in Turin.

Neto last played for Juventus in May 2017, when he was part of the side that beat Lazio 2-0 in the Coppa Italia final. More than nine years on, the Brazilian is in line to start again in black and white, with first choice Guglielmo Vicario being rested for the visit of the Cypriot side to the Allianz Stadium.

His most recent competitive outing came on 30 May with Botafogo, as Football Italia noted after Wednesday’s press conference. Since then he has been working as cover, a role he took on after joining as a free agent at the end of September.

Juventus moved for Neto after Kamil Grabara ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in training on 19 September, only days after keeping a clean sheet on his debut against NEC. The club confirmed his return on 28 September with a contract running until 30 June 2027.

Asked what drew him back, Neto explained that he had been looking for a next step that genuinely meant something to him. “Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open,” he said, in comments reported by ilBianconero, which carried the press conference live. He added that he is enjoying his work and is in Turin to help, whatever the coming months bring.

Opening the press conference, he described his feelings simply: “It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team.”

Neto was asked about Vicario, who is on loan from Tottenham and has been Luciano Spalletti’s regular choice in goal. He kept his answer short: “I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper.”

The veteran also spoke warmly about the younger players around him. He said their eagerness to contribute was infectious and that the squad has the quality, will and determination it needs. On the goals Juventus have conceded this season, he pointed to a side that is still developing, with several players new to Serie A and finding their way. His own focus, he said, is on training at full intensity every day while the team looks for balance and consistency.

Juventus go into matchday five fifth in the league phase standings with ten points from four games. Omonia have won two and lost two. Neto warned against taking them lightly, saying they are a strong side who break forward with real quality, and revealed he knows Omonia’s Fabiano from his years in Brazil.

He also stressed that Europe brings its own demands, noting that Juventus always carry a responsibility to compete to win in every tournament they enter.

Interest in the meeting was already strong after ticket sales for Omonia passed 35,000 last week. Next up in Serie A is the trip to Como, where both sides go in without suspensions.

For Neto, the night is a chance to add to the 22 appearances he made in his first spell, when he won two league titles, two Coppa Italia trophies and a Supercoppa Italiana as Gianluigi Buffon’s understudy.

#1378. Marching on together, Ao? Leeds look to tie down Tanaka to a new deal after shining this season - with Dominic Calvert-Lewin also in extension talks amid Man United interest

By SIMON JONES and TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 14:08 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:18 EST, 25 November 2026

Leeds United are in advanced talks with Japan international Ao Tanaka over a new contract.

The 28-year-old midfielder is close to agreeing terms on a deal that will keep him at Elland Road until 2029 with his current contract due to expire in the summer of 2028.

Leeds have lost only 10 games out of the 66 Tanaka has started since joining the club from Fortuna Dusseldorf in 2024. He has had an impressive start to the current campaign, becoming a key figure in Daniel Farke's side, starting in nine of Leeds' 11 Premier League matches. They currently sit seventh in the table.

Leeds have already tied down Ethan Ampadu to a four-year deal while Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson all signed new contracts during the summer transfer window.

Talks are also expected to progress over a new deal for Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has been linked with a move to bitter rivals Manchester United as they look to bolster their striking department.

Discussing Tanaka's form ahead of their emphatic win over Chelsea at the weekend, Farke said: 'It was a big ask for him after spending many years on second-tier level in Germany or here in the Championship.

Ao Tanaka (left) is in advanced talks with Leeds United over signing a new contract until 2029

Leeds are also in talks with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin over a new deal to stay at Elland Road

'Last season was his first year in the top league. I think he’d shown glimpses of his potential, but he needed to find a bit of consistency. I would agree that he is finding this during the season.

'It was not always a 10 out of 10 performance but I think it's important for a player, once you're mature, that on the weaker days you're still a six or a seven out of 10, and this is what he's doing.

'So perhaps even on the more challenging days, he's at least solid and plays first of all with good confidence, like he always does, but also with a seriousness to be consistent and to work for the team, also against the ball, strong in the duels.

'Still sometimes in decision-making and in front of goal he can be a bit calmer. But overall, I think he's on a really good path to mature more and more. And if you do this, then you become more and more important for us. And we're all happy that he is in such a shape at the moment.'

#1377. Roma draw 2-2 at PSG as Malen’s late penalty adds to Juventus’ December challenge

Roma came from behind to draw 2-2 with holders Paris Saint-Germain, with substitute Donyell Malen scoring a 78th-minute penalty. The leaders' rivals above Juventus showed the depth of their squad less than a month before they host Spalletti's side.

Roma left the Parc des Princes with a point and with their reputation enhanced. Mario Hermoso gave them the lead against the European champions. Paris Saint-Germain turned the game around through an Illia Zabarnyi header and an Ousmane Dembélé penalty.

In Europe, Malen’s spot-kick was his fifth goal. Across all competitions, it marked his 17th strike of the campaign, from 16 appearances. It came days after he scored four times in Roma’s 5-1 win at Parma. Yet he did not start in Paris, and neither did Paulo Dybala. Gian Piero Gasperini said he left Malen out because of the number of games he had played for Roma and the Netherlands.

That a reshuffled Roma could take a point in Paris says plenty about their squad. Luis Enrique’s side had not dropped points since a home defeat to Monaco on 4 September.

The result does not fix Roma’s European position. The club lists the game as Matchday 5 of the league phase. Roma have one win, two draws and two defeats so far. Under the format, clubs finishing 9th to 24th enter the play-offs, while 25th to 36th are knocked out. The top eight go straight into the round of 16.

That leaves Roma with work to do in a crowded December. Their next Champions League match is at home to Sporting CP on 8 December, kicking off at 21:00. They then travel to AEK Athens on 19 January and host Lille on 27 January 2027.

Domestically, Roma’s form has been strong. Their league record shows nine wins and three draws, with 36 goals scored and 11 conceded, Corriere dello Sport reported.

For Spalletti’s side, the schedule offers some contrast. After that European fixture, Roma play the derby away to Lazio on Sunday 13 December at 12:30. That leaves them six days between the derby and the visit of Juventus. Before travelling to Rome, Juventus are away to Como on 29 November. Udinese and Monza then come to Turin in Serie A, on 6 December and 14 December respectively.

Whether Roma’s European commitments take a toll remains to be seen. The evidence from Paris suggests Gasperini can rotate without a sharp drop in quality. Malen’s form, from the bench or from the start, will be a central concern for Juventus.

The two sides meet in round 16 of Serie A on Saturday 19 December 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1375. Three above a 7, two below a 5: Fan player ratings for Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan

AC Milan rose from the canvas floor on the outskirt of Athens on Thursday night, coming from two goals down to beat Olympiacos 4-2.

With 50 minutes on the clock, Milan trailed by two goals after a Mike Maignan own-goal and a strike from Jota Silva. However, Omari Hutchinson inspired a comeback, halving the deficit with a great solo goal then setting up Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround.

Diego Moreira scored on the break in the final seconds of added time to add a fourth and make sure of the victory, which boost the Rossoneri back into the top 24 with three games to go.

Looking at what our readers gave the players for the win in Piraeus, there is a real mixed bag of scores which in many ways matches the two-sided nature of the performance.

Starting with the negatives, Koni De Winter really struggled all night and played a stray pass for the second goal, which resulted in an average score of 4.5 out of 10 from our readers. Pervis Estupinan didn’t do much better, getting a 4.6.

Sankhoun Diawara had one of his tougher nights and got a 5, while Goncalo Ramos only got a 5.3 and Ardon Jashari also fell below a passing grade, but only just (5.9). Mike Maignan was scored a 6.1 and Adrien Rabiot a 6.2.

Then we get to the difference-makers: Diego Moreira averaged a 7, Alphadjo Cisse a 7.3 and Omari Hutchinson one of our highest grades of the season, with an outstanding 9 out of 10.

The subs were as follows: Yunus Musah got a 6.6, Christian Pulisic an 8.1, Fikayo Tomori a 7/1, Filippo Terracciano a 5.9 and Christian Comotto a 6.1.

#1374. Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a big moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke said. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”

Forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Murillo had Forest’s best opportunity two minutes into injury time after cutting inside the penalty area but could not find the top corner.

"That was magic!" What a goal this would have been from Murillo?! 😩 https://t.co/D07lB7hN47

Another defeat will only add to their concerns and Glasner needs to quickly find a solution or face another relegation battle.

It does not promise to get easier immediately, either, with Manchester City, Chelsea and Brighton up next in the league at home, but there were encouraging signs here, despite the club sitting in the bottom three.

Glasner said: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

“It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”

We knew the margins would be really small. They are extremely well coached and organised. The longer the game goes on they gain more belief. We had to be so patient - and clinical when we got the chance. The way they were defending, they were more comfortable. But we have players with different qualities and can adapt to what the game is delivering.

We have another three big chances that should be goals. That is the difference, you have to be clinical. If we keep generating them, they will come.

Let’s enjoy the win, because it was a very tough one. And then, on Wednesday, we have an incredible game against Bayern Munich away [in the Champions League].

When you see their goal it’s deflected otherwise, it’s straight to the gloves of Matz Sels. You have periods in football where you feel everything going against you and then there are periods when things are on your side.

Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.

And having this coolness, not to worry too much because I can see good performances and not good results. The results will come if the performances stay good.

Noni [Madueke], Jurrien [Timber], Mikel [Merino] was brilliant when he came on and Viktor [Gyokeres] really changed the game - all of them did and that’s what we need. Noni obviously the highlight because he scored the goal and that’s the difference.

Sometimes you can get frustrated with teams who are difficult to break down. First half we didn’t have a shot on target and that’s something we discussed. We had another two big ones in the second half but the only one on target we had was a little deflection and it’s in.

Great reaction [after scoring goal], to have the will to defend a really open and difficult and stressful situation.

We knew it would be a tough game, it always is against Arsenal. They have a good team. But we feel we can change the result, maybe a draw, maybe a win. Now we have to put it in the past and focus on the next match.

We have a good manager and I think we are still getting his ideas. We changed everything in our system this season. It is difficult but after three or four months we keep improving and I think we are close to reaching our best.

If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd so we know that we’re going to start some and finish some and for me it’s the same mentality every time I just want to create or score.

Amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win.

We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. Great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.

32 - Since Mikel Arteta became Arsenal manager in December 2019, they have had the joint-most 1-0 wins in the Premier League of any side (32, level with Everton). Stereotype. https://t.co/nD7C3j7Xjw

Arsenal dig out a very ugly victory, and one they probably did not warrant. Forest can take positives from their performance, primarily the solidity of their defending and a more threatening Delap performance.

Forest cling on by their fingernails with Arsenal flooding forward, but Merino’s pass to Saka in the box was underhit. Chris Wood and Hudson-Odoi are now on for Forest as they chase an equaliser. Cunha and McAtee the Forest players to depart.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Ndoye are Dominguez are the Forest players coming off in a double change, replaced by Kalimuendo and Sangare. Forest will be worth a point if the game continues this way.

Declan Rice with a shank out for a throw when he was looking for Saka. Kalimuendo is ready to come for Forest, so Glasner is introducing another forward.

Delap with a tame shot from distance, before Timber instigates a more dangerous Arsenal attack with a reverse pass into Odegaard. The ball is worked to Madueke and his deflected cross is headed away. Saka wants a throw but the linesman has other ideas. Still no goal despite more endeavour in this half.

Arsenal building some pressure, and they have another corner. Arteta signalling that he wants to make the change before the corner is taken and here come the changes: White for Timber, Havertz for Gyokeres and Merino on for Bruno Guimaraes.

Gabriel meets Rice’s delivery, but he fails to direct his header on target.

Excellent defending from Gabriel up against Ndoye in the right channel, but it was another promising moment for Forest in this second half. Madueke then isolates his man one-on-one, and wins another corner.

Timber, Merino and Gyokeres are all ready to come on for Arsenal.

The game is see-sawing, Arsenal have a corner after Calafiori fed Madueke down the left and his cross was blocked. Sels punches away, and then Odegaard loses some patience and tries to find Calafiori with a pass that is not on.

Saka and Rice lose duels when fishing for fouls and Forest have another corner. Arsenal’s performance level has certainly not improved since half-time.

Arsenal clear, but Odegaard blocks a cross and Forest win a second corner in quick succession. Excellent goalkeeping from Raya to claim, and he bowls the ball forward quickly, but Forest snuff out the danger against Madueke.

The first half was an attack against defence session for long periods but Arsenal know they are in an arm wrestle now. Forest far more aggressive, and the crowd are more involved. But that could open up avenues of space. White with a really poor pass towards Saka which is astray.

Arsenal have a corner of their own after breaking from Raya’s gloves. Much more open game so far.

Forest deal with Saka’s delivery, and there was a very brief VAR check for a handball penalty. Nothing doing.

Madueke looking dangerous, receiving a Gabriel ball over the top and dashing inside but his shot was blocked.

Delap’s shot from a tight angle is then deflected wide. Forest corner, from which Murillo’s header loops into Raya’s gloves. Forest showing more attacking ambition.

Liam Delap is producing a very decent centre-forward performance.

Madueke and Rice not one the same wavelength, before Delap does well to win a shoulder to shoulder with Gabriel only to slice his cross behind for an Arsenal goal kick. Sums up the lack of attacking quality in the game.

Forest have another free-kick in a shooting position after Havertz is penalised for blocking a long shot with his hand. McAtee’s effort from the free-kick is scooped miles over the bar.

Both teams looking livelier in the early exchanges of the half, but Forest’s counter-attack was the more dangerous, with Liam Delap doing well to hold on to the ball and whipping a cross into the box that was just ahead of Williams.

Noni Madueke replaces Eberechi Eze, so a more natural wide player on his stronger foot on Arsenal’s left flank.

Frustrating first half for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta will be demanding more from his attacking players.

Arsenal have not registered a shot on target so far and their delivery from set-pieces has been poor.

Forest look relatively comfortable and had the best chance of the half with a shot from Dan Ndoye which was saved by David Raya.

Are we heading for a hat-trick of 0-0 draws at the City Ground between these two teams?

A very uneventful 45 minutes which has been played at the pace of a pre-season game at times. Similarities with the last two fixtures between these teams at the City Ground, and Arsenal’s games against Leeds and Lille this week. They put their foot on the pedal after half-time in both games, and they need to do the same here.

Guimaraes is off the pitch, and there will be more than two minutes added now as a result of his treatment. Forest win a corner, but Havertz heads away at the near post.

Just the two minutes of added time to play.

Liam Delap wins a free-kick in a shooting position for Forest after Arsenal were caught with numbers forward. Big moment for the home team, this. Calafiori was caught on the ball again, he has not had the best of games.

Williams and McAtee are over the free keek, which is around 25 yards out, left of centre.

Williams blasts the ball into Bruno Guimaraes, who goes down and stays down after taking the shot flush in the face.

More incisive from Arsenal, with Rice punching the ball into Odegaard and then on to Havertz but the angle was always against him and the German could only shoot into the side-netting. Forest have defended very well, overall. Although they have been deep for the most part, they have jumped and pushed out at the right times to stop Arsenal accessing the box.

Glasner and Arteta dish out some instruction while there is a stoppage in play to deal with a hand in the face that troubled Schlager. Can either side find a breakthrough before the break?

David Raya claimed that Forest corner with ease and the game has now resumed its pattern. Forest retreating into their shape, and Arsenal passing in front of them. Schlager penalised for a foul on Saka, the home fans not happy with the decision, I think because Saka was going away from goal.

Rice clips in a menacing delivery, but Havertz skewed his header wide from seven or eight yards. Good chance, Arsenal’s best so far.

More Arsenal probing but the small details are letting them down: Eze’s return to Odegaard forced his team-mate to check, and then Odegaard’s touch was heavy after a wall pass from Guimaraes.

Delap does well to make a nuisance of himself at the other end, and his long-range shot deflects behind for a corner.

Strong from Konsa to win the ball, drive out of defence and win a foul. Rice with a well-weighted scoop over the Forest defence for the run of Ben White, but he skewed his cross behind for a goal kick.

Arsenal with another corner. No doubt they have been the game’s dominant force when it comes to possession and territory, but there has been a lack of cutting edge so far. Saka goes for the near post again but Forest deal with it. The home crowd groan at Sels for not releasing the ball quickly in search of a break.

Arsenal work the ball across their midfield with Guimaraes, Rice and Odegaard all involved, and a dangerous Saka cross is headed behind for a corner.

Scramble! The near-post flick on caused chaos and Konsa’s goal-bound backheel was blocked, but the ball would not quite drop for Ben White to score a tap-in.

After two successive goalless draws here between the two clubs, this is following a similar script so far.

It’s a very tight affair with Arsenal enjoying more of the possession but Forest seemingly happy with that and content to them on the break.

Bruno Guimaraes has made a bright start for the visitors.

Forest’s best attacking moment of the game and it comes from an Arsenal mistake.

Calafiori just had to play a five-yard pass back to Gabriel but scuffed it, and Munoz pounced. Running at the Arsenal penalty area, Munoz’s cross was deflected to the back post and the ball found it’s way to Ndoye. Decent reverse shot through legs, but Raya had it covered and tipped around the post.

From the corner, Forest are penalised for a foul.

Arsenal continue to have Forest penned in their own half, very difficult for the home team to play through the midfield or over Konsa and Gabriel so far.

Saka produces his first successful dribble to beat Williams, and the left wing-back trips him at the expense of a free-kick and a booking. Rice’s delivery from the right was uncharacteristically poor.

Munoz tries to drag Forest up the pitch to apply some pressure on Arsenal but he is penalised for a shirt pull on Gabriel. The atmosphere sounds pretty sleepy, a result of some tepid Arsenal possession and Forest’s bad home record.

Forest making sure they have numbers around Saka whenever Arsenal funnel attacks down their right, which is almost always their preferred side.

Neat from Guimaraes in midfield to turn and find Saka with some earlier service, and Sels tips his cross away from danger.

Delap and Ndoye waiting for a slip-up or counter-attack but they are feeding on scraps at the moment. Arsenal yet to carve out a proper chance, though.

It’s already pretty clear that one of the key duels today will be between Gabriel and Liam Delap.

Forest’s record signing Delap has already let Gabriel know he’s in the game with his physicality.

Cute pass from Bruno Guimaraes to break the Forest midfield line and find Odegaard, but strangely the Arsenal captain could not sort his feet out to control the ball and back a clean pass. Then Williams defends well against Saka from an Arsenal attacking transition.

Pretty subdued start from Forest. The crowd’s spirits were raised there by Delap chasing down Konsa who had the deal with the sun his eyes, but the Forest striker pushed him in the back.

Arsenal enjoying all of the possession so far, and most of it has come in Forest’s half. One or two players on Arsenal’s right/Forest’s left struggling with the low evening sun. Havertz did get in behind but his cross into the middle was too strong.

Arsenal get the game under way, and play short from kick-off.

There will be a degree of pressure on birthday boy James McAtee today to make an impression.

With Morgan Gibbs-White injured, McAtee is likely to take the No 10 position and continue his redemption arc.

McAtee has been revitalised since the arrival of Oliver Glasner and this is a big afternoon for the former England under 21 international.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

We'll wear black armbands this afternoon, as we join our hosts in remembering nine-year-old Nottingham Forest supporter, James Kerry, who passed away earlier this month following a brave battle with cancer. Rest in peace, James ❤️ https://t.co/YFIXnCfJJX

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

An FA Cup defeat in Jan 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparked a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

Yet Arsenal have secured two wins in a row since that defeat at Brighton, without being truly at their fluent best, and will be confident against a Forest team without injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White.

Remembering Arsenal's last visit to Nottingham Forest... Mikel Arteta was FUMING with his side 💥💥💥 #AONArsenal #NFOARS https://t.co/A6MGTfYlDG

Dominguez and Schlager are the preferred midfield pair in the 3-4-2-1 with Sangare on the bench. McAtee and Ndoye will support Liam Delap in attack. Much attacking responsibility on Munoz at right wing-back, who also has the cavalier Calafiori on his side of the pitch, which could prove fireworks.

Forest XI: Sels, Jair Cunha, Diomande, Murillo, Munoz, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams, McAtee, Ndoye, Delap

No surprise that Havertz, Odegaard, Saka and Calafiori are restored to Arsenal’s Premier League starting XI having started on the bench in mid-week. Eze over Madueke and Guimaraes over Lewis-Skelly were closer calls for Arteta. Ben White comes in for Timber, with Arsenal managing the minutes of both right-backs.

Arsenal XI: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Eze

Subs: Meslier, Mosquera, Timber, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Sunday starters 👊 🤝 Presented by @deel

Fascinating stuff from Sam Dean this morning, who has profiled a member of Mikel Arteta’s inner circle who is not listed on Arsenal’s website. Germán Castaños, an expert in innovation who has written multiple books on alternative thinking, has become a key member of the team. Things started with a phone call with Nicolas Jover, then a meeting with Arteta and now he splits his time between Argentina and London. Find out more about Arsenal’s mystery man and his methods here.

In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. Conceição, rated 8.61, was involved in three of the goals and had 7 shots and 4 key passes before being replaced with 86 minutes played. Boga and Ekhator also scored, the latter in 66 minutes on the pitch, while Neto made 4 saves.

Juventus had 60% of the ball and completed 570 of their 619 passes, against 351 of 410 for Omonia. They had 23 shots to 13, with 9 on target to 5, and finished with expected goals of 2.42 to 1.13. Kaminski made 5 saves in the Omonia goal.

The win is Juventus’s second in a row with four goals, following the 4-0 victory over Venezia, and leaves them unbeaten in five matches in all competitions since their defeat to Genoa. In that run they have also beaten Napoli and AZ Alkmaar and drawn with Fiorentina.

For Omonia, it is a second defeat in their last four matches, after a draw with Apoel Nicosia, a win over Anorthosis and a loss to NEC Nijmegen.

Markus Krösche will soon begin his work as AC Milan’s new Head of Football, but Timmo Hardung will not be joining him.

It has not been a well-kept secret that Milan have wanted to welcome Krösche as the new head of the management since the summer. Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall a few months ago, but the German has since left his position and now seems all set for a new adventure in Italy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Compensation has been agreed to release him fully from Eintracht, and the only question mark swirling concerned whether he would be joined by his right-hand man Hardung, with whom he has worked for years.

“I wanted to focus on Timmo Hardung, in the sense that I would like to specify a situation linked to the Rossoneri organisation that already exists, what he will become and what could be in the future,” he said.

#1371. Jude Bellingham scores 'the best goal of my life' as his stunning long-range volley helps Real Madrid come from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026

Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

SENSATIONAL JUDE BELLINGHAM 🤯Bellingham gives the hosts the lead with a magnificent volley 🔥 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WdP6ULx8wE

Jude Bellingham (right) scored a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

'I'm not one for smashing the ball too hard and it was a nice moment and important for the win as well.'

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a new Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week

2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week

3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week

4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week

5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week

However, they didn't have it all their own way as PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute from the penalty spot, with 37-year-old captain Ivan Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a resounding victory from Bellingham's pass, underlining the Spanish side's credentials as serious contenders to take Paris Saint-Germain's crown.

#1368. Mariani to referee Como v Juventus, with Como still without a win under him

Maurizio Mariani of the Aprilia section will take charge of Como v Juventus at the Sinigaglia, a direct fight for the Champions League places. Como have never won with him in charge, and his recent record has brought friction with Inter and with Francisco Conceição.

Maurizio Mariani of the Aprilia section will referee Como v Juventus at the Sinigaglia on Sunday 29 November at 20:45. The AIA named Peretti and Perrotti as his assistants. Marinelli will be fourth official. Pezzuto is on VAR, with Meraviglia as AVAR.

Como have never won with Mariani in charge. For Juventus, the appointment comes in a direct fight for the Champions League places. Spalletti’s side are sixth and Como fifth, so a win at the Sinigaglia would close the gap on a direct rival.

Mariani’s name came up last season in Milan prosecutors’ wiretaps in the so-called ‘Arbitropoli’ case, Tuttosport reported. Those conversations discussed referees said to be welcome or unwelcome to Inter. Inter president Beppe Marotta also strongly criticised a penalty Mariani gave Napoli against Inter on 25 October 2025. He called it a ‘rigorino’, meaning a soft penalty.

The Juventus link is more direct. Francisco Conceição has had a goal disallowed by Mariani. The paper calls the referee a nightmare for the Portuguese winger. That disallowed goal was not the only troubled meeting between the two.

Both video officials will also work the night before. Pezzuto is assistant VAR for Torino v Lazio on Saturday 28 November at 18:00. Meraviglia runs the VAR for Inter v Genoa later that evening.

After 12 rounds, Como have won eight, drawn two and lost two. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10. Juventus have won six, drawn three and lost three, with a 19-12 goal record. Spalletti has called the Como game a key moment after the win over Omonia.

Como will come into Sunday’s game with two more days of rest than Juventus. Spalletti countered that players returning from injury let him plan for the Como game as well. Before the Omonia game, Nico González and Kalulu had not recovered, along with the long-term absentees.

#1367. Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan: Five things we learned – a breakout night and a glaring issue

AC Milan went into their Europa League fixture against Olympiacos in need of a win to get the ball rolling, and win they did.

The eventual 2-4 scoreline only tells part of the story, as Ruben Amorim’s side had to battle back from two goals down. Lorenzo Pirola’s header drew what was officially an own-goal from Mike Maignan, then Jota Silva doubled the lead after a slack pass from Koni De Winter was punished.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then came the Omari Hutchinson show. The Englishman gave Milan hope with a wonderful solo goal, before turning provider for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround. Diego Moreira’s late goal on the counter made sure of a very important three points.

So, the Diavolo return to Italy with smiles on their faces, cultivating the hopes of a play-off spot and keeping the top eight dream alive too. Ivan Stoev has picked out five major talking points from a dramatic night on the outskirts of Athens.

Omari Hutchinson has had mixed performances when given the opportunities since his arrival in the summer and the feeling is that he had plenty of work to do in order to justify the hefty optional price tag on his loan contract. Games like the one against Olympiacos are just the type of opportunities for the attacker to prove his abilities.

The Nottingham Forest loanee didn’t get off to the best start as Milan struggled in the opening 45 minutes with their opponents pressing very high and aggressively. This starved him of possession in a central role and he didn’t get the ball to his feet much, let alone with space to run at.

In the second half, however, Hutchinson moved to a wider role on the right flank and he immediately started causing trouble for the Greeks.

In the 56th minute it was an impressive solo run by the Englishman that started Milan’s comeback as the winger picked up the ball in his own half and carried it all the way to the opponent’s penalty box, before cutting onto his left foot and beating the keeper with a tidy finish in the far post.

Milan fez uma grande reviravolta na segunda parte em casa do Olympiacos, com Omari Hutchinson em destaque. https://t.co/RsOgYVqrP7

Seven minutes later Hutchinson continued to cause trouble down that flank. This time around he found Cisse with a lovely cross and the youngster made no mistake to bury it and bring the scores level.

The former Arsenal academy man wasn’t finished yet though: in the 71st minute he provided yet another inviting cross into the penalty box which found Pulisic, who applied a lovely volleyed finish to make it 3-2.

Hutchinson then continued to be a menace in transition as he showed relentlessness even in the dying minutes. A corner was cleared and he picked up possession, somehow beat a man and ran with it, getting the ‘hockey assist’ for Moreira’s goal.

It was an absolutely brilliant second-half performance and if he finds continuity then that option to buy might just before more appealing, or at the very least a re-negotiation to keep him permanently. The issue is that the Olympiacos owner also owns Forest, and he saw that display first-hand.

The goals Milan conceded were quite preventable yet again. The feeling is definitely growing as January approaches that the back line needs a true leader in the middle of a defence that continues to be error-prone.

Mario Gila has looked like a bargain of a signing and he has been superb, but he is playing mostly as a right-back/outside centre-back. Strahinja Pavlovic remains a key player as well, but the same applies as with Gila just on the left side.

Koni De Winter is just not a man that you can trust to anchor the rearguard to a high level most weeks. He’s had some stellar performances – the game against Inter comes to mind – but he often follows up those performance with some shocking ones.

Matteo Gabbia is definitely better in terms of leadership and keeping things tidy, but we will need to wait and see if he features in Amorim’s long-term plans. He’s been injured for quite a while too, so a reacclimatisation period will be required.

Sankhoun Diawara also looked very shaky in Greece, but this in itself proves a point because the idea cannot have been for him to start as many games as he has. It just further signals that someone who can play down the middle and steady everything could be the difference this season and beyond.

Ardon Jashari got his first Milan goal at the weekend in the win over Frosinone. Then, the unfortunate injury to Luka Modric leading up to the Olympiacos game meant he was given the chance to prove himself, after a few shaky performances this season.

Excluding a few misplaces passes in the first half, the Swiss international was solid enough. There wasn’t anything flashy but also no errors leading to goal, which was a relief.  The stats say that he had 77 touches, completed 58/64 passes (91%), had 1 big chance created, 2 tackles, 7 recoveries and 1 clearance. He also won 2/2 aerial duels and 2 ground duels, committing just 1 foul.

Speaking of chances being seized, it’s worth giving a shoutout to Fikayo Tomori who came on for a struggling De Winter. Milan looked much more solid with the Englishman on the pitch as he showcased his athleticism but also his experienced reading of the game.

The professionalism shown by Tomori must be respected given the centre-back was excluded from the squad in the summer and put on the transfer market. He worked hard to prove that he deserves to stay and to play. Now, the next mission is to earn what currently seems like an unlikely renewal.

In the first half Milan were struggling with the high press and the limited space, so they had limited chances going forward. The second half was a completely different story especially with Yunus Musah and Pulisic coming on for Estupinan and Goncalo Ramos.

We have already mentioned Hutchinson ran the show, but Pulisic was also crucial as he scored an impressive volley which is hard to execute by any standard,  and he then goal the assist that made the final 4-2. He should’ve really scored another one, but we’ll give him a well-earned pass.

Moreira was also heavily in the mix and at times he was frustrating with his end product being lacking, though the direct nature of his pace and dribbling were a joy to watch again. Having a player who picks up the ball and says ‘Fine, I’ll do it’ is really refreshing. His defensive effort as a wing-back was not lacking either.

Cisse all in all had a quiet game yet found his name up in lights on the scoreboard for a 10th time this season with a tidy headed finish. The knack that he has for being in the right place at the right time is something that is so impressive in a 20-year-old. A pay rise could be on the way to fend off calls from England.

We have to give the coach his flowers too, don’t we. The first half wasn’t good but it was still better compared to some other European performances this season. The goal was very preventable, but the Rossoneri did well not to fold under the pressure Olympiacos were applying.

In the second half the coach made two changes which improved the team quite a bit, though one of them was forced as Ramos was injured. Amorim revealed after the game that he knew the Greek side couldn’t keep up their high press for 90 minutes, which would yield spaces to attack in the second half.

Shifting Hutchinson to the right was also the correct choice, as was taking off De Winter for Tomori, and also letting Cisse play as a centre-forward. Depending on how Ramos is, he might have to do the same in Cagliari.

Finally, it is worth mentioning the attitude was completely different as opposed to the game against Ferencvaros. The desire and belief that the game could be turned around offers some encouragement that this team cannot just get into the knockout stages, but can give anyone a game if they show up.

#1366. Europe in shock after Doué’s injury, the English press dismantles JJ Gabriel’s entourage

Last night, PSG picked up another victory in Nice, but no one was really talking about the result after the match. The reason is obviously the serious injury of Désiré Doué. While he had just scored to give the Parisians the advantage, the French international collapsed alone after twisting his right knee. The images are terrible: Doué screams in pain, hides his face and finally leaves the pitch in tears, on a stretcher. But what is also striking this morning is that Doué’s injury is shaking up the European press. In Spain, A.S. explains that “his knee set off all the alarms at PSG“, while Sport title : “Doué’s terrible injury slows down the party“. Mundo Deportivo also mentions “a Parisian victory overshadowed by worry“. In Italy, La Gazzetta dello Sport speaks of a real shock and insists on the parallel with Kvaratskhelia’s injury. Even the English press returns to these images of Doué being evacuated in tears. An emotion which therefore goes far beyond French borders.

A controversy is causing a lot of talk in England: the management of JJ Gabriel’s career. THE Daily Mail publishes a particularly virulent column against Ali Barat, the agent of the young 16-year-old prodigy, announced very close to Real Madrid after his departure from Manchester United. At the heart of the criticism, a promotional video published to announce the arrival of Gabriel in his agency. We see in particular a reference to the Ballon d’Or, before the young player declares on camera: “I am epic“, in other words “I am exceptional“. For the English newspaper, this communication is completely disproportionate for a boy who has not yet played a single minute among the professionals. Email also questions the role of those around him in his departure from Manchester United and the risks of such early exposure.

In Italy, Donyell Malen continues to panic the counters. The Dutch striker absolutely crushed Parma with a quadruple in Roma’s 5-1 win. Four shots, four goals, and now sixteen goals in fifteen matches. Gian Piero Gasperini’s team also has 36 goals after twelve days of Serie A, its best total at this stage since the 1950-1951 season. Enough to start dreaming very seriously of the title. Malen has simply been on cloud nine since his arrival in Italy, a sparkling form which is enough to worry PSG, three days before the clash between the two teams in the Champions League.

#1365. THE BREAKDOWN: How Florian Wirtz suddenly became the most powerful creative force in the Premier League - from Andoni Iraola's perfect tactics to Liverpool's Bradley Barcola effect

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:37 EST, 25 November 2026

After Florian Wirtz trudged off the field just over an hour into Liverpool’s defeat by Manchester City in October, sacrificed following Ryan Gravenberch’s red card, Jamie Carragher had once again seen enough of the £116million man.

‘I think he needs to come out of the team,’ said Carragher post-match. ‘I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again.’

Fast forward six weeks, and Wirtz was running the show for Liverpool as they put four past Manchester United in poor Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge, topping a stellar performance off with a goal and an assist. Carragher hailed the German’s stunning first-half volley as ‘a goal Dennis Bergkamp would have scored’.

How things change. This was a performance, even against an abysmal 10-man United, that showed Wirtz was ready, at last, to seize the big occasions.

Because, for so long, he wasn’t ready. Carragher was not alone in his earlier assessment, one shared by countless frustrated Liverpool fans. There was a feeling that this slight, wispy technician had the tools to flourish in the slower-paced Bundesliga, or even for Liverpool in the Champions League, but would, perhaps, remain unable to shine amid the rough and tumble of the Premier League.

Wirtz managed five goals and four assists in the Premier League last season and added only one assist this term before that City game. Since then, he’s come to life. Four assists and a couple of goals in the league with another one of each in the Champions League, a tally he will hope to add to on Wednesday evening against Club Bruges.

Florian Wirtz has suddenly sprung to life as a Liverpool player and is making his critics eat their words

Wirtz scores a majestic flick against Manchester United on Sunday

Since that City defeat, Wirtz is getting into dangerous positions more often. He is having more touches in the opposition box, more shots in the opposition box, playing more passes into the opposition box and creating more than twice as many chances from open play.

Wirtz boasts a league-high 29 of those this season, and 20 of the chances have come since that City game.

The last player to create more than the 10 open-play chances Wirtz managed against United was David Silva in 2015. Wirtz created nine against Brentford, too, in the first league match after the City defeat, meaning he’s the only Premier League player on record (since 2003-04) to create nine or more chances from open play in multiple games in the same season. Wirtz did it twice in five weeks.

Let’s nip this one in the bud early. It is clear, of course, that Jurgen Klopp, the legendary former Liverpool manager now Germany head coach, has got a tune out of Wirtz in recent months. The pair, according to those who follow the national team, are very close.

‘Wirtz is a once-in-a-century talent,’ was Klopp’s assessment last year, while he later remarked that he was ‘shocked’ by how good Wirtz was in their first training session together.

The 23-year-old has shown it in matches, too, with four goals and an assist in his last four games for Germany, including a brace last week against the Netherlands.

This has fed a narrative of how Klopp has been the one to unlock Wirtz’s powers. Klopp deserves credit, naturally, but he is also helped by having the freedom to give Wirtz what he needs: space.

‘What do I need to be at my best? Ideally, a lot of space in every game so I can do what I want!’ said Wirtz after scoring one and setting up the other in Germany’s 2-0 win over Serbia in October.

He was half-joking, laughing as he said it, but he’s right. Technical creators like Wirtz thrive on space. He’s been able to have more of that in international football, with Klopp even playing him as a false nine to give him all the creative freedom he needs. He leads the press but the midfielders behind him do the bulk of the dirty work to allow Wirtz, the star, to shine.

Wirtz’s performances with his country have helped grow his confidence, but it would be deeply unfair on Iraola to suggest Klopp’s blueprint is the one now being copied.

Even if Liverpool and Germany play a similar style, it is much, much harder to give players freedom in the Premier League.

But if anyone was going to find a way to do it for Wirtz, it was Iraola.

Arne Slot could never work it out. By the end of his tenure, he’d played Wirtz as an attacking midfielder, stuck him on both flanks and thrust him up front. It was a conundrum he just couldn’t solve.

Iraola's Bournemouth side were one of the hardest-working, highest-pressing teams in the division but his system was still able to allow the likes of Justin Kluivert or Junior Kroupi to create and drift into pockets of space to set the attacking tempo.

For Iraola, it was always going to be Wirtz. The German has started every league game, all of them in the No 10 position.

He’s always led the way off the ball – only three players have won possession more often in the final third this season – but Iraola has been finding different ways to get the best out of him with the ball, too. Against Brentford, he shifted Rio Ngumoha inside almost to play as a second No 10 beside Wirtz, which helped create space for him to set up Liverpool's equaliser.

Having Alexis Mac Allister behind him allows Wirtz to concentrate on being the creative heartbeat, while even Dominik Szoboszlai has played noticeably deeper since returning from injury.

Andoni Iraola has started Wirtz in every league game, all of them in the No 10 position

Szoboszlai isn't the only one. Another aspect of Germany's game that has helped Wirtz is lining up alongside strikers who like to drop deep in Kai Havertz and Nick Woltemade, leaving space for Wirtz to attack.

In recent weeks, especially against United, Liverpool striker Alexander Isak has been doing the same. It was Isak doing exactly that which led to Wirtz’s goal.

Isak (below, in possession) drops in, plays the ball out wide to Ngumoha and Wirtz sprints into the box to get on to the end of the cross.

Alexander Isak dropped into midfield and sprayed the ball wide to Rio Ngumoha before Wirtz's goal against United

Isak missed much of last season through injury but his all-round play is much better attuned to Wirtz's game than those who played alongside him for most of 2025-26, including Hugo Ekitike.

One of the most devastating aspects of Iraola’s Bournemouth was how quickly players flooded forward when they attacked.

His Liverpool side is starting to do the same which, in turn, helps get the best out of Wirtz.

Last season under Slot, the likes of Cody Gakpo and Mo Salah would often tuck in instead of bombing forward out wide and Milos Kerkez, one of the most attacking full backs in the division under Iraola at Bournemouth, rarely did the same under Slot.

Now, Liverpool’s wingers are flying. This season under Iraola, Liverpool are averaging more ‘fast breaks’, how Opta define counter attacks, and shots from them than in any campaign under Slot or even the ‘heavy metal’ Klopp.

Wirtz has attempted seven through balls this season, one of the highest tallies in the division. Since the City game in particular, he has tried to play passes with purpose into the box.

Wirtz was creating chances in the first six games of this season but only a few of them were penetrating passes into the box

The German's chances created in the last five games, since the City defeat, show how many balls he is playing into dangerous areas

The rapid Bradley Barcola starting to find his feet since his £123m move has been a huge help to Wirtz.

Of Wirtz’s 20 open-play chances created since the City game, a quarter of them have been for Barcola.

Having those runners out wide like Barcola and Ngumoha is so helpful for the German. As he drives forward with the ball against United (below), he has three runners ahead of him with even Szoboszlai bursting forward. Wirtz has so many options and eventually slips in Isak for a great chance.

Liverpool had wide runners driving forward against United, helping Wirtz create chances and split their defence

You can see from the average position map from the game (below), just how attacking Liverpool’s wingers – and Kerkez – were, albeit, granted, against 10 men for most of the contest.

The average position map of Liverpool's players against United shows how high up the pitch they played

Wirtz has had a run like this before, around this time last year. During December and January, he racked up four league goals and three assists – having not managed a single one until then – only to notch one of each for the rest of the Premier League campaign.

You get the sense, though, with his confidence growing under managers for both club and country who want to play his way, that he might just keep shining this time.

#1362. FIFA: the FFF should formalize the candidacy of Philippe Diallo on Tuesday

Philippe Diallo’s candidacy for the presidency of FIFA should take a new step this Tuesday. After receiving unanimous support from UEFA this Monday, the boss of the French Football Federation must now obtain official validation from the FFF executive committee. An expected step to fully launch his campaign against Gianni Infantino, whose new mandate will be submitted to the vote of the 211 member federations on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco. The French leader, who retains his functions at the head of the FFF during this campaign, will thus represent the candidate supported by the European body in this presidential election.

For Philippe Diallo, this meeting marks the start of a campaign which promises to be particularly demanding. At the head of FIFA since 2016, Gianni Infantino has a lot of support across the different confederations. According to several echoes reported by RMC Sportthe outgoing president would already count on 80 to 90 votes acquired. The Frenchman will have to convince beyond the European circle to give an international dimension to his candidacy. His appointment comes after several avenues explored by UEFA, including those of Luis Figo and Arsène Wenger, which ultimately did not come to fruition. The ratification expected on Tuesday by the COMEX of the FFF will formalize its entry into this race for the presidency of FIFA.

#1361. 'You can't escape from it': Rasmus Hojlund opens up on the suffocating pressure of playing for Man United - and reveals Bruno Fernandes and Diogo Dalot are 'looking forward to change' under Mauricio Pochettino

Published: 05:31 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 06:12 EST, 25 November 2026

Rasmus Hojlund has laid bare the suffocating pressure of playing for Manchester United and given his insight into what Mauricio Pochettino’s squad will be suffering while marooned in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Dane was back in town this week after spending two seasons at United, mocking Manchester City fans when scoring the opener of Napoli’s 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night.

Hojlund secured a £38million permanent move away from Old Trafford in the summer but remains in touch with plenty of old team-mates and believes the lack of equilibrium at the club has contributed to a steady decline.

‘There are so many people following the club around the world and you can’t really escape from it,’ Hojlund said.

‘It is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad. It is all about trying to be in that middle. I had both the highs and the lows there.

‘The pressure is part of the club, it comes with playing for United. There has been a lot of change but hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio.’

Rasmus Hojlund mocked Man City fans after scoring for Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday night

A United supporter, Hojlund laughed off the idea that the club is in a relegation scrap despite their worst start to a season since 1972. And the 23-year-old revealed that the players were ready for ‘change’ following the sacking of Michael Carrick.

‘I spoke with Bruno [Fernandes] and Diogo [Dalot] during the international break and they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,’ Hojlund added.

‘I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best. I am sure they will turn it around this season. They have got a lot of quality. They have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals.

‘It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top. The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth was in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.’
